newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 9.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Senior security sources on Tuesday claimed the Irish Republican Army's admission of responsibiltiy for the double car bomb attack at Lisburn marked a decisive "return to war".
- The Irish government will attempt to cap the fees of solicitors and barristers for the Hepatitis C Tribunal to avoid another hugely expensive judicial inquiry.

- The Irish government on Tuesday invited key organisations to the opening of national pay pact talks later this month as a new report urged tax cuts of up to one billion Irish pounds over the next three years.

- If Ireland is to continue its spectacular growth in tourism after the year 2000, it must plan for the long term as less European Union funding will be available to aid investment, the Irish Tourist Industry Confederation warned.

- The umbrella body governing the loyalist paramilitary groups is expected to meet shortly to consider retaliation for the Irish Republican Army's car-bomb attack on the British army headquarters in Lisburn, County Antrim, on Monday.
- Income tax could be reduced by 800 million Irish pounds over three years if unions and employers sign up to a new agreement to succeed the Programme for Competitiveness and Work.
- The priority in income tax change should be to reduce the tax burden on lower and middle-income earners, according to the latest report from the National Economic and Social Council (NESC).
- Two Dublin criminals, one who had connections in the past with a splinter republican group, are the prime suspects in the murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin on June 26.
